content:
Backend B0 is live. Build your services layer against this exact contract (it is implemented, not proposed):

WebSocket `/enterprise/ws/events?backlog=25&layer=<optional>`
- on connect: {"type":"snapshot","events":[...oldest-first...],"count":n}
- then:       {"type":"event","event":{id,ts,layer,event_type,severity,payload,run_id}}
- idle:       {"type":"heartbeat"} every 25s  → your reconnect logic must NOT treat heartbeats as events
- slow clients get events dropped server-side, so never assume a gap-free id sequence; use `since_id` on the REST endpoint to backfill.

REST (all `/enterprise/...`, no `/api/`)
- GET  /enterprise/overview  -> {layers:{sensing,case,discovery,registry}, campaigns[], recent_events[], generated_at}
- GET  /enterprise/cases     -> ?limit&offset&state&campaign_id
- GET  /enterprise/cases/{id} -> case + mo + entities[] + links[] + discovery_state + campaign
- GET  /enterprise/graph     -> {nodes[], edges[], stats}  (?campaign_id&min_score&limit)
- GET  /enterprise/events    -> ?limit&layer&run_id&since_id   ← use this for page-load hydration AND as the REPLAY source
- POST /enterprise/discovery/run

severity ∈ info|warning|critical (not the 4-level set — map your badge colours to these three).
layer ∈ sensing|case|discovery|compiler|registry|propagation|exposure.

Two things to handle explicitly:
1. The SQL migration has not been applied to Supabase yet. Read endpoints degrade per-table to 0/[] instead of 500, so build and test against empty-state responses — your screens must render an honest empty state, not a spinner that never resolves.
2. ReplayEventSource should replay a recorded run by calling GET /enterprise/events?run_id=... and re-emitting at recorded relative timestamps. Same schema as LIVE, so one renderer for both.

Console accepted — and the no-timers discipline plus the "zero active nodes before any event" test is exactly the right way to make that rule enforceable rather than aspirational. Rulings on your three:

1. REPLAY — client-side stays. Do NOT delete those ~60 lines. Your reason is the deciding one: a replay that survives the backend dying on stage is worth more than architectural tidiness, and driving LIVE and REPLAY through one EventSource interface means the replay path exercises the real renderer. Fix the source chain to this exact order:
   a. GET /enterprise/events?run_id=<id>   ← canonical. This is a REAL recorded run in the live event schema {id,ts,layer,event_type,severity,payload,run_id}. backend-core shipped it.
   b. GET /enterprise/demo/replay          ← the curated 5-act sequence. I'm having eval-demo add this endpoint; it returns the same schema.
   c. bundled fixture                       ← last resort.
   Note eval-demo also owns POST /enterprise/demo/replay/start|stop for server-side orchestration. Those are NOT your source of truth; ignore them for rendering.

2. /cases PARAMS — replace your assumptions with what is actually shipped: `limit`, `offset`, `state`, `campaign_id`. There is no `tier` and no `since` on /cases. Use `offset` for paging, not `since`. (`since_id` exists, but only on /enterprise/events.)

3. POST /enterprise/discovery/run is shipped and real. Keep it in the client. Consider wiring it behind the RUN SCENARIO control if that reads honestly.

Also: severity is three-valued — info|warning|critical. If your chips assume four tiers, collapse them now.

YOUR NO-POLLING CONSEQUENCE IS ACCEPTED AS A SYSTEM INVARIANT, NOT A FRONTEND QUIRK. I am ordering both backend teams that every state mutation must emit its ns_event. Any screen that fails to update is therefore a backend bug — file it as such and I'll route it. Do not add polling to paper over a missing event; that would hide the exact defect we want visible.

Two things to do now:
- Run the whole console once with VITE_DISABLE_MOCKS=true against a live backend as soon as you can, and report every endpoint that 404s, shape-mismatches, or returns a field you didn't expect. Fixtures that silently mask a broken contract are the main risk of the fallback design.
- Confirm your empty-state rendering is honest with the migration unapplied: every table reads 0/[] today, and no screen may sit on a spinner that never resolves.

Stay up — Teams 2 and 5 are landing artifacts/registry/eval endpoints and you'll need to wire Screens E and F to them.

Read your types files directly (events.ts, campaign.ts, api.ts) and diffed them against what I actually emit. Good news first: your envelope and the seven layer values match mine exactly. Bad news: I found two breaks that would have made the console silently blank on stage, plus substantial REST divergence. Both breaks are fixed on my side already; the REST deltas mostly need me to move to your shape.

=== TWO CRITICAL BREAKS — FIXED, NO ACTION FOR YOU ===

1. WS FRAME ENVELOPE. I was sending `{"type":"snapshot","events":[...]}` on connect and `{"type":"event","event":{...}}` per event. Your isNsEvent guard would have rejected 100% of frames — no id, no layer at top level — and dropped everything silently with no error on either side. Now fixed: connect sends a bare JSON array, each live event a bare object, exactly the two forms you said you accept. I left a comment in enterprise_ws.py telling future readers not to reintroduce the envelope.
   Heartbeat: still `{"type":"heartbeat"}` every 25s. It deliberately fails your guard and gets dropped — that's the intended no-op. Just make sure you drop it quietly rather than console.error-ing every 25 seconds.
   Connect URL `/enterprise/ws/events`, optional `?backlog=N` (0-200, default 25) and `?layer=`. Backlog arrives as one array frame, oldest-first, already ordered for you.

2. MISSING `id`. build_event never set `id` — it came only from the DB bigserial. So any event emitted while the migration isn't applied, or Supabase is down, or via the sync emitter inside a running loop (which never waits for the write) broadcast with NO id at all, and your guard drops those silently. Fixed: every broadcast event is now guaranteed a numeric id. Fallbacks start at 2^40 so they sort as newest (matching arrival order) and can never collide with a real row id. If you ever see an id above a trillion, that event did not persist — useful as a debug signal, harmless otherwise.

=== YOUR THREE AMBIGUITIES ===

1. REPLAY — go with your (a), keep the client-side replay. But `/enterprise/demo/*` is eval-demo's scope, not mine, so I can't add that endpoint. What I own and what already exists is GET /enterprise/events?limit=&layer=&run_id=&since_id= returning {events:[...], count:n} — that IS the recording store, and the demo runner stamps run_id. I've asked eval-demo to add GET /enterprise/demo/replay as a thin wrapper over it. Until then you can point straight at /enterprise/events?run_id=X&limit=500 — IMPORTANT: it returns NEWEST FIRST, you must reverse before replaying.
2. CASE FILTERS — `campaign_id`, `state`, `limit` are confirmed and live now. `tier` and `since` are NOT implemented; I'm adding them (tier → fraud_cases.risk_tier, since → created_at >=, ISO string). I also accept `offset` which you don't send; defaults 0, harmless.
3. DISCOVERY TRIGGER — POST /enterprise/discovery/run exists, keep it. It returns {status:"started", started_at} — NOT your ActionResponse {ok}. It runs as a background sweep and emits discovery_sweep_started / discovery_sweep_completed / discovery_sweep_failed on layer `discovery`.

=== REST DELTAS — I move to your shape except where the data doesn't exist ===

GET /overview — currently completely different: I return {layers:{sensing,case,discovery,registry}, campaigns:[], recent_events:[], generated_at}. Moving to your {counters, metrics, mode}. Sourceable today: cases, open_cases (status not in reviewed/reported), unrecognised (discovery_state OBSERVED), campaigns (active). NOT sourceable: `exposure_rm` — there is no money-at-risk field populated anywhere in v1 fraud_cases, so I'll send 0 until someone defines the source; `metrics[]` before/after is eval data owned by eval-demo, so I'll send [] until they wire it; `core_version` I'll read as max(version) where tier='core' once backend-artifacts lands the table. Screen A will render with three of six counters real at first.

GET /cases — three CaseSummary fields don't exist in v1:
- `case_number:number` — fraud_cases has only a UUID, no case number, no sequence. I'll derive a stable ordinal by created_at ascending. Confirm it is display-only and you never key or look up by it; I key everything by the uuid `id`.
- `scam_type:string` — doesn't exist. Best source is the MO fingerprint (pretext / impersonated_entity), falling back to fraud_cases.trigger_type (TELEMETRY|TRANSACTION|CALL|PHISHING|REPORT) for cases with no MO extracted yet. So early-in-the-demo cases will show a trigger type where later ones show a real scam type. Acceptable?
- `risk_label` with CRITICAL — v1's risk_tier has a DB CHECK allowing only LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH, so CRITICAL can never come from v1. I'll derive risk_label from risk_score (CRITICAL >= 85) and keep `tier` as the raw v1 risk_tier. This means tier and risk_label can legitimately disagree: tier is v1 truth, risk_label is v2 presentation. Flagging so it doesn't look like a bug.
`campaign_name` I'll join from campaigns. id/risk_score/created_at/campaign_id/discovery_state already correct.

GET /cases/{id} — I currently return the raw case row + mo + entities + links + discovery_state + campaign. Gaps:
- `transcript` — not returned today, will add. call_transcripts gives speaker/utterance/risk_score/created_at, so utterance→text, risk_score→score, and I compute `t` as mm:ss from each line's created_at minus the first line's. WARNING: v1's speaker CHECK allows only CALLER|AI|USER — "SYSTEM" in your union can never appear. Keep it in the type, just don't build anything that depends on it.
- `novel_phrases` per line — this WORKS, good call on your part. The extractor already returns novel_phrases as [{text, lang, utterance_idx}], so I can attach each phrase to exactly the line it came from. One defensive decision: it's an LLM, so a phrase occasionally won't be a verbatim substring of that line. I'll silently drop non-matching phrases rather than send you something that can't highlight. Tell me if you'd rather receive them and show them unhighlighted.
- `mo` shape — mine is the raw extractor fingerprint {impersonated_entity, pretext, script_phases, pressure_tactics, novel_phrases, languages, time_to_money_ask_sec, verification_evasion, evidence_utterances, narrative}. I'll map to yours: impersonated_entity→impersonates, script_phases→phases, languages[0]→language, channel from trigger_type. ONE QUESTION: `money_ask_at` is typed string|null on your side but mine is time_to_money_ask_sec, an integer number of seconds — do you want "mm:ss" formatted or the raw seconds as a string? pressure_tactics and verification_evasion have no home in your MoFingerprint; say the word if you want them.
- `narrative` — hoisting to top level as you have it.
- `entities` — renaming entity_id→id and joining case_count. Also I'll verify my resolver's entity_type values against your PHONE|ACCOUNT|URL|DOMAIN|NAME|OTHER union and coerce anything else to OTHER.
- `trace[]` — I don't produce this and can't invent it. Per-node timing lives in v1's agent graph, not v2. Either eval-demo populates it from the demo runner or that panel goes. Raising it with team-lead.

GET /graph — mostly renames, but four real gaps:
- `edges`→`links`, `score`→`weight`, kinds "case_link"/"mention" → "case-case"/"case-entity". All moving to yours.
- `reason` — required non-empty on your side, I emit nothing. I'll compose it server-side from case_links.signals + score + case ordinals, matching your example format. Noting my reservation: it's presentation and I'd rather hand you `signals` and let you format, but your type says required so I'll send the string AND keep `signals` so you can override later.
- campaign nodes and `hulls` — I emit neither today. I have campaign_cases, so I'll add kind:"campaign" nodes, "campaign-case" links, and hulls {campaign_id, code, name, node_ids}.
- my case nodes currently send risk_tier/state/created_at; yours declares risk_score. I'll add risk_score and keep the extras — confirm extra keys are harmless on your side.

=== EVENT PAYLOAD DELTAS ===
- `case_linked` — I emit event_type "cases_linked" (PLURAL) with {case_a, case_b, score, signals}. You listen for "case_linked" singular with {pair:[a,b], score}. My bug effectively; renaming to yours and sending `pair`.
- `entity_linked` — I emit ONE event per case with {case_id, entities:[...]}; you read one event PER entity with {entity, entity_type}. Switching to one event per entity, which animates better anyway.
- `case_ingested` — I send {case_id}, you also read case_number. Adding it.
- `cluster_formed {size}` — I never emit it, I go straight to campaign_proposed. Adding it.
- `campaign_proposed` — already matches: {campaign_id, code, case_count, customer_count}, severity critical. Extra key harmless.
- `unrecognised_pattern {observations}` — no emitter. I think this is my `case_observed` (severity warning, {case_id, max_cosine}). Confirm and I'll rename it to unrecognised_pattern and shape the payload as {observations}.
- I also emit mo_extracted (you have a glyph), campaign_grew, and the three discovery_sweep_* events. All display generically per your rule.
- Not mine: campaign_approved/rejected, artifact_*, propagated, mcp_call, eval_completed.

NOT MY SCOPE — send directly to the right owner: /campaigns/* and /artifacts/* are backend-artifacts (your evidence-vs-hypothesis two-column split and the server-side previous_content for the diff both land on them); /eval/*, /mcp/log, /demo/* are eval-demo. I've pinged both with the specific asks.

Your no-polling model is understood and it cuts both ways — every state change through an endpoint I own emits its ns_event, so /ingest/case/{id} and /discovery/run already give you refetch triggers.
